title: Clare
hookLine: Francis's friend who founded the Poor Clares and, tradition says, faced down soldiers holding the sacrament

cards: Soldiers are coming over the wall of a small convent outside Assisi. Inside are women with no weapons, and their abbess is sick in bed. Here's what the old account says she does.
She has herself carried to the door. She asks for the sacrament, the consecrated bread kept in a small box, to be set in front of her. She bows down before it and prays.
And the soldiers, the story says, turn back and leave. The woman at the door is Clare, Francis's friend, whose sisters came to be called the Poor Clares.

teach.h: OUT OF HER FATHER'S HOUSE AT NIGHT.
teach.b: Clare grew up in a noble family in Assisi, Francis's town. She heard him preach and wanted the life he lived: poor, simple, given to God.
The Legend of Saint Clare says she slipped out of her family's house at night and went to Francis and his brothers, who cut her hair as a sign she was leaving the old life behind.

When her relatives came to drag her home, she held onto the altar and showed them her shorn head, and they let her be. She settled at a little church called San Damiano, and other women came, her own sister among them.
Their life was enclosed, prayerful and poor, and for years Clare asked church leaders to let her sisters own nothing at all. Back to the door.
In some tellings, as she prays before the sacrament, a voice answers that God will always guard them.

Whatever you make of it, the story says something about Clare: her defense was not a wall or a sword, but stillness and prayer before what she held most holy. Catholics and other Christians honor her as a saint.
The same Legend tells of her last days.
Lying ill, she speaks to her own soul: go forth in peace, for you will have a good escort. The woman who walked out of her father's house at night ends by sending her soul out the door, without fear.

how: The Poor Clares live an enclosed life of prayer in convents around the world, and Catholics and some Anglicans keep a feast day for Saint Clare.

games.why: the story says she was carried to the door, bowed before the sacrament and prayed, and the soldiers turned back.

practice: Stand in a doorway, any door, feet on the floor and hands loose, and breathe. Think of what comes through doorways in your life, news, people, worry, and neither block it nor rush out to meet it.
If you pray, hold in mind someone facing something frightening today; if not, let the breath slow and the doorframe hold you up.
